summary: The 12-month Enrollment component covers activity from July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2018, and is reported by eligible postsecondary institutions at the institution level. It covers undergraduate and graduate enrollment or instructional activity over the full 12-month period, making it useful for institutions with nontraditional calendars or short-term programs. The tables differ in whether they report unduplicated students or instructional hours, and the instructional-activity table has a separate odd-year collection rule.

The Completions survey covers awards and related program offerings reported for July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2018 by institutions in the IPEDS Completions reporting universe. It is institution-based, with records organized either at the institution level or by program and/or award level, and covers certificates and degrees plus associated demographic and distance-education information. No even- or odd-numbered-year reporting restriction applies to this 2018 collection.

Fall Enrollment reports institution-level student counts and related fall measures for eligible IPEDS postsecondary institutions. Traditional-calendar institutions report as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with program-specific or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. Most tables may contain multiple records per institution because students are classified by table-specific categories, and applicability varies by institution type, academic calendar, and program offerings.

The Finance component is collected annually during the winter collection cycle for the institution’s fiscal year ending between July 1, 2017, and June 30, 2018. The unit of observation is the postsecondary institution, and the universe is active Title IV-participating institutions eligible to report institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and related finance information. Institutions report on the accounting-standard form appropriate to their control and tax status; beginning with fiscal year 2016, detailed functional expenditures and natural classifications for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are no longer available.

Graduation Rates data were collected from November 14, 2018, through February 6, 2019, reporting student outcomes as of August 31, 2018. The survey covers eligible Title IV postsecondary institutions with qualifying undergraduate programs and reports outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts, rather than all enrolled students. Cohorts and outcomes are reported separately by institution, program length, cohort type, and graduation or transfer status; the applicable cohort years and completion windows vary by table.

Human Resources data report institution-level staff records for eligible postsecondary institutions, covering fall payroll staffing, academic-year salaries, and fall new hires. Fall staff counts are generally measured as of November 1; the 2018 new-hire period runs November 1, 2017, through October 31, 2018, while salary data cover academic year 2018-19. Detailed instructional-staff and new-hire tables are restricted to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices; other tables have broader applicable-institution coverage.

The Institutional Characteristics survey is collected annually in the fall for the academic year, with institutions reporting institutional characteristics and charges according to the applicable IPEDS reporting dates and calendar-system rules. The institution is the unit of observation, covering active postsecondary institutions in the IPEDS universe; Title IV-participating institutions are required to report, while other eligible institutions may be included. Some fields apply only to particular institution types, program calendars, or reporting situations.

The Student Financial Aid survey collects institution-level data for July 1, 2017–June 30, 2018 from eligible postsecondary institutions participating in federal Title IV programs. Reporting covers students enrolled during the academic year and the financial aid or benefits administered through the institution, with institution-specific counts and dollar amounts rather than student-level records. The survey is collected annually; no even- or odd-year availability restriction applies.
